title: American Elm: Great American Elms You Can Visit
meta_description: Central Park's west side once held about 500 American elms; by 1985 a survey counted 23. Four survivors mapped, all of them in the park.
intro: Central Park's western edge once carried about 500 American elms. A New York Times survey counted 23 of them in 1985, and one of the four trees mapped here is on that shortlist, standing on Central Park West opposite the natural history museum and wider than it is tall. Dutch elm disease reached the city in the 1930s and took the great majority of the elms that had shaded nearly every street in it, which is why every survivor now reads as an event. A pair east of the Mall grow straight out of exposed Manhattan schist, roots spread flat across rock over a billion years old. The avenue on the Mall itself has been replanted three times, because foot traffic kept compacting the soil, and the row you walk under now went in during the 1920s. All four are in Central Park.
